Distributed Consensus: Raft achieves consensus by electing a leader via randomized election timeouts.
The leader handles all client requests and replicates log entries to followers.
A log entry is committed once a majority of nodes acknowledge it.
On leader failure, a new election starts after the election timeout expires.
Split-brain is avoided because only one candidate can win a given term.
Log compaction via snapshots bounds disk usage independently of log length.
Joint consensus allows safe cluster membership changes without downtime.
Paxos variants (Multi-Paxos, Fast Paxos) trade latency for throughput.
Key-Value Store Design: LSM-trees batch random writes into sequential I/O using an in-memory memtable.
When the memtable reaches its size limit it is flushed to an immutable SSTable.
SSTables are periodically merged via compaction to bound read amplification.
Bloom filters per SSTable reduce unnecessary disk seeks for negative lookups.
Block cache holds recently accessed data blocks to serve hot reads in memory.
Write-ahead logging ensures durability: the WAL is fsynced before ack.
Column families allow independent compaction schedules for different data.
Leveled compaction bounds space amplification at the cost of write amplification.
Attention Mechanisms: Scaled dot-product attention computes Q*K^T / sqrt(d_k) then softmax * V.
Multi-head attention runs h parallel attention heads and concatenates outputs.
Grouped-query attention (GQA) shares K/V heads across query heads to reduce KV cache size.
Multi-latent attention (MLA) compresses K/V into a low-rank latent vector.
Flash Attention fuses the softmax and matmul into a single CUDA kernel.
Sliding window attention limits each token to a fixed local context window.
Rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) encode position via rotation in complex space.
KV cache stores computed key/value tensors to avoid recomputing during decoding.
Caching Strategies: LRU eviction removes the least recently accessed item when capacity is reached.
CLOCK approximates LRU with a circular buffer and reference bits.
TinyLFU uses a frequency sketch to admit only high-frequency items.
Write-through caches update both cache and backing store on every write.
Write-back caches defer backing-store writes, improving write throughput.
Cache-aside (lazy loading) loads data into cache on first miss.
Two-tier caching places hot data in DRAM and warm data on NVMe SSD.
Prefix caching deduplicates KV tensors for shared prompt prefixes across requests.
GPU Memory Management: CUDA unified memory enables automatic page migration between CPU and GPU.
HBM2e provides ~3.2 TB/s bandwidth vs ~50 GB/s for DDR5.
Tensor parallelism shards weight matrices across GPUs to reduce per-device memory.
Pipeline parallelism assigns consecutive layers to different devices.
Activation checkpointing trades compute for memory by recomputing activations.
PagedAttention manages KV cache in fixed-size pages like OS virtual memory.
Memory pooling pre-allocates large CUDA buffers to avoid repeated malloc/free.
Mixed precision (BF16/FP8) halves or quarters the memory footprint of weights.
Networking and RPC: gRPC uses HTTP/2 for multiplexed, bidirectional streaming RPCs.
Protocol Buffers serialize structured data compactly with schema evolution.
RDMA bypasses the CPU for memory-to-memory transfers over InfiniBand or RoCE.
TCP slow start ramps up the congestion window exponentially until loss.
QUIC multiplexes streams over UDP, eliminating head-of-line blocking.
Service mesh (Envoy/Istio) offloads TLS, retries, and circuit breaking from apps.
NCCL implements collective operations (AllReduce, AllGather) optimized for GPUs.
Zero-copy networking passes buffer ownership to the NIC without CPU memcpy.
Scheduling and Queue Management: Shortest-job-first minimizes average wait time but requires knowing job length.
Work-stealing lets idle threads take tasks from busy thread queues.
Weighted fair queuing assigns bandwidth proportional to each flow's weight.
Token bucket rate limiting smooths bursty traffic to a sustained average rate.
Chunked prefill splits long prompt prefills across multiple scheduler steps.
Continuous batching groups decode steps from different requests into one batch.
Preemption evicts low-priority requests to free KV memory for high-priority ones.
Speculation decoding runs a small draft model to propose tokens for the large model.
Database Indexing: B+ tree indexes store sorted keys in leaf nodes linked for range scans.
Hash indexes provide O(1) point lookups but do not support range queries.
Bitmap indexes compress membership information for low-cardinality columns.
Covering indexes include all projected columns to avoid heap fetches.
Partial indexes index only rows satisfying a predicate, reducing size.
GIN (Generalized Inverted Index) supports full-text and JSONB containment queries.
BRIN stores min/max per block; effective when data has natural clustering.
Adaptive radix trees (ART) combine memory efficiency with cache-friendly lookups.
